mongo.title: MongoDB connection
mongo.description: Connection settings for your MongoDB database.

host.title: Host
host.description: The full connection URL of your MongoDB database.

database_includes.title: List of databases to include
database_includes.description: A list of databases names to include in the discovery process. If this list is empty, all databases available on your MongoDB instance will be included.

batch_size.title: Batch size
batch_size.description: The number of documents to fetch in a single batch. Setting this to a smaller number helps reduce the overload on the system, although the extraction time will be higher.

cursor_timeout.title: Cursor timeout (minutes)
cursor_timeout.description: Server-side cursor timeout in minutes. Set to 0 to disable timeout, which prevents CursorNotFound errors on long-running syncs. Note: 0 is not supported on Atlas free/shared tiers. When not set, uses MongoDB's server default (10 minutes).

max_parallel_streams.title: Max parallel streams
max_parallel_streams.description: The number of streams to sync in parallel. Defaults to 1 (sequential). Increasing this value can significantly reduce total extraction time for pipelines with many collections.

cdc_image_mode.title: CDC post-image handling (Log Based)
cdc_image_mode.description: LOG_BASED (CDC) replication requires changeStreamPreAndPostImages to be enabled on every source collection. Without it, update events silently misattribute state (events end up carrying the document's 'current' state rather than the state at the time of the event), making SCD Type 2 / audit histories incorrect. Enable per collection with: db.runCommand({collMod: '<coll>', changeStreamPreAndPostImages: {enabled: true}}). This setting does not decide whether pre-/post-images are required (they always are) — it only controls where enforcement happens. 'whenAvailable' (default, migration-friendly): correctly-configured streams sync; misconfigured ones are skipped with a clear per-stream error and a consolidated summary. 'required': MongoDB itself refuses to open the change stream if any watched collection is not configured — use once every collection is confirmed set up, so the pipeline fails fast at startup if someone later disables the feature.
